statement: For a finite-image Artin representation rho with no invariants, if L(s,rho) is holomorphic and nonzero on Re(s)>1/2 then, for every complex |c|<=1, the damped Euler product D_c(s)=prod_p det(1-c rho(Frob_p)|I_p (Np)^{-s})^{-1} continues holomorphically without zeros to that half-plane.

statement: For a nontrivial irreducible Artin L-function and one fixed irrational real 0<c<1, meromorphic continuation of D_c to Re(s)>1/2 is equivalent to holomorphic nonvanishing of L there. A rational c=a/b in lowest terms forces b to divide every divisor order in that half-plane.

statement: The A5 virtual character reg−5χ4 has negative χ4 coefficient but nonnegative inner product with every induced linear character from every subgroup. Thus all Hecke-induced linear positivity inequalities alone do not force Artin holomorphy. This is an abstract character counterexample, not an actual L-order realization.
